guitar.modelsText: Kay Thin Twin (modified with DeArmond pickup)
models: Kay Thin Twin (modified with DeArmond pickup)
guitar.evidence: Elmore James is famous in blues history for his slide playing on a modified Kay Thin Twin guitar with a DeArmond pickup, well documented in blues guitar literature.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown; this is a well-known fact among blues historians.

tone.target: crying slide blues with raw fuzzed amp bite
tone.profile: crying slide blues with raw fuzzed amp bite
tone.summary: A vintage-inspired chain featuring Fuzz for initial grit, followed by a UK 50 or US Deluxe to capture the small combo breakup, finished with subtle Room reverb for space.

rig.name: Elmore James - The Sky is Crying - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray notes typical of blues recording.
Provide the core 'fuzzy buzzy sustain' and raw bite required for slide blues.
Placeholder for potential mild grit boost (kept inactive as Fuzz is primary).
blocks.gap: The Green OD was considered but bypassed in favor of the dedicated Fuzz unit to achieve a more raw, sustained tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the 'cranked small combo' and tweed/Valco style amp breakup, providing classic blues grit.
Provide a classic British voicing that complements the UK 50 amp model.
Sculpt the tone to emphasize single-note clarity and bite, while avoiding scooped mids.
Kept inactive as the focus is on raw tone and sustain, not modulation.
Add the requested 'slight room' ambience without muddying the raw blues tone.

improvements.summary: Swap IR for a more natural, open-air cabinet sound to better match the raw blues/slide feel.

proposals.recommendedAsset: open air 2x12 or tweed cab IR
proposals.reason: The UK Vintage 4x12 is too British; a smaller, more open sound fits the raw blues vibe.
